newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand fell prey to a fresh onslaught of dollar demand on Thursday as jitters ahead of the July 1 foreign exchange control relaxations increased.
By 1400 GMT, the rand had lost a cent to trade at 4.4815/4830 against the dollar -- its weakest level since May 16 -- from 4.4715/4745 on Wednesday.
"Last night and this morning we saw demand for dollars and it has been fairly well bid all day," a trader said.

Dealers said the approach of July 1 -- the date when individuals will be allowed to invest offshore in line with government's exchange control relaxations -- was making players increasingly nervous as they tried to guage what amount of capital would leave the country.
That combined with market talk that the Reserve Bank was keen to allow the rand to weaken was also spurring demand for the U.S. unit.
"The feeling we are getting is that the Reserve Bank is trying its hardest to let (the rand) slip a bit without letting it run away," the trader said.
Market talk early on Thursday was that the central bank had been in the market buying dollars, contrary to general perceptions that it was prepared to offer at the 4.4850 level.
"It's getting increasingly nervous. There is no panic but people are saying the rand is a bit overvalued and has to weaken so lets buy dollars," the trader added.
On the day the 4.4850 level held.
"There were exporters in at around 4.4850. Whether the Reserve Bank was in I don't know but I got the feeling that he was around."
On Friday, dealers said the rand looked set to weaken further, possibly probing the 4.4850 to 4.4875 levels.
"I think we will probably close around 4.4875 tomorrow and open above 4.49 by Wednesday next week."
Dealers said the main level the market was wary of was the 4.50, where there large stop losses are believed to have accumulated.

Against the crosses, the rand was last quoted at 0.3853/3858 marks from 0.3878/3882 marks overnight, at 25.7541/7937 yen from 26.0432/26.0831 yen and at 7.3030/3101 on sterling from 7.2947/3045 previously.
